def:joint-packet.title: Finite source-complete joint packet
def:joint-packet.note: Encoded. RepresentedJointPacket (Lambda, V, M, E) bundles the represented data (J1)-(J5) in the coordinates of the central type decomposition: the common carrier is Carrier = Sigma lambda, (Fin 4 x V lambda) x M lambda (the paper's H_X up to the unitary decomposition of (J3), which the structure fixes as coordinates); (J1) the faithfully represented external Clifford factor A_Cl = M_4(C) acts as extAction a = blockDiagonal' (a (x) I (x) I), a unital *-representation (extAction_mul/one/conjTranspose) faithful when some sector is nonempty (extAction_injective); (J2)/(J3) the kinematic typing algebra A_type = ⊕ I_4 (x) B(V_lambda) (x) I_M is intAlgebra = range intAction (mem_intAlgebra_iff), commuting with A_ext (extAction_commute_intAction); (J4) the directed incidence graph is (src, tgt : E -> Lambda) with represented incidence operators Y e : C^4 (x) V_{s e} (x) M_{s e} -> C^4 (x) V_{t e} (x) M_{t e}, placed on the (t e, s e) corner of the carrier by incidenceOp (blockEmbed); (J5) the mixed words are the elements of actionAlgebra = jointActionAlgebra A_ext A_int Y (def:action-algebra), star-closed; multiplicityAlgebra = its commutant. def:action-algebra.title: Joint typed action algebra
def:action-algebra.note: Statement encoded (new version renames the generators: A_act = C*(A_Cl, A_type, Y_e, Y_e^*) instead of C*(A_ext, A_int, ...)). jointActionAlgebra A_Cl A_type Y : Subalgebra C (Matrix n n C) is starAdjoin (the least star-closed unital subalgebra = the finite-dimensional C*-algebra generated) of A_Cl ∪ A_type ∪ range Y with the incidences Y_e represented as matrices on the common carrier; the two generating sets are arbitrary parameters, so the encoding is unchanged by the renaming. thm:trinity.title: Factor obstruction and typed decomposition
thm:trinity.note: Proved for general n (Fin m, m >= 1) and an arbitrary finite sector set. Setting: phi : M_m(C) ->a B(H) a unital *-copy of M_m(C) (AlgHom with phi(X^*) = phi(X)^*), H finite; A_type a unital *-closed subalgebra commuting with phi. factor_commutant (eq:factor-commutant): a UNITARY U : C^m (x) K -> H (reduction unitary U(e_i (x) xi) = e_{i0} xi built from the matrix units phi(E_ij) and an isometry onto Ran phi(E_00); general-m version of the Clifford reduction) with phi(X) = U (X (x) I) U^* and M_m' = {U (I_m (x) y) U^*}. factor_obstruction: I_m (x) B(K) has trivial centre, so a subalgebra with a non-scalar central element is not the full commutant. trinity_typed_decomposition (eq:trinity-H, eq:trinity-Aint, eq:trinity-C, eq:trinity-Cprime): there are a finite sector set Lambda, nonempty V_l = C^{I l}, M_l = C^{J l} and a unitary T : C^m (x) (+)_l V_l (x) M_l -> H with phi(X) = T (X (x) I) T^*; A_type = T (I_m (x) (+)_l B(V_l) (x) I_{M_l}) T^* (actionBlockSet); C = C*(phi(M_m), A_type) = T Q T^* for exactly the Q all of whose (i,j) coefficient blocks lie in (+)_l B(V_l) (x) I, i.e. M_m(C) (x) (+)_l B(V_l) (x) I = (+)_l B(C^m (x) V_l) (x) I_{M_l}; C' = T (I_m (x) (+)_l I_{V_l} (x) B(M_l)) T^* (multBlockSet). Proof: A_type = I (x) A' with A' a *-closed subalgebra of B(K) (comap of the lift); reciprocal_wedderburn on A'; C' computed directly from the generators; C by the finite double commutant theorem. Non-vacuity example: M2 (x) I on C^2 (x) C^2 with commuting I (x) M2. Disclosed rendering: the carrier is written C^m (x) ((+)_l V_l (x) M_l), canonically (distributivity) equal to (+)_l C^m (x) V_l (x) M_l; under it I_m (x) (+)_l B(V_l) (x) I = (+)_l I_m (x) B(V_l) (x) I, M_m (x) (+)_l B(V_l) (x) I = (+)_l B(C^m (x) V_l) (x) I and I_m (x) (+)_l I (x) B(M_l) = (+)_l I_{C^m (x) V_l} (x) B(M_l); this reindexing is not spelled out in Lean.

def:incidence-coefficients.title: Intrinsic incidence coefficient space
def:incidence-coefficients.note: Encoded. For an edge e of a represented joint packet P (Y_e : K_s (x) M_s -> K_t (x) M_t, K = C^4 (x) V), B_e = RepresentedJointPacket.coefficientSpace P e := range of the linear slice map phi |-> (phi (x) id)(Y_e) (sliceLinearMap, functionalSlice), phi ranging over all linear functionals on B(K_s, K_t); mem_coefficientSpace_iff is literally eq:intrinsic-incidence-coefficients, and it is a linear subspace by construction. eq:general-incidence-expansion: coefficientSpace_eq_span_blockSlice (matrix-unit HS orthonormal basis) and coefficientSpace_eq_span_of_basis / range_sliceLinearMap_eq_span_of_basis (Y_e = sum_a D_a (x) F_a in ANY basis (D_a) of B(K_s, K_t), HS-orthonormal or not, gives B_e = span{F_a}). The coefficient-space quiver: vertices = the index data M_l; forward arrows j = inl e carry Y_e and adjoint arrows j = inr e carry Y_e^H (ArbitraryIncidenceDuality.quiverSrc / quiverDst / quiverArrow), with arrow spaces arrowSpace = span of all functional slices (= B_e, resp. B_e^* = {B^H : B in B_e}); QuiverEnd / mem_quiverEnd_iff give its endomorphism space and reduce it to the finitely many coefficient equations. The generic slice layer (functionalSlice, blockSlice, sliceSpace, arrowSpace) is in MultiplicityQuiverArrows.

def:typed-multiplicity.title: Typed multiplicity algebra
def:typed-multiplicity.note: Encoded for a represented joint packet P (RepresentedJointPacket, def:joint-packet) with incidences Y_e : K_{s(e)} x M_{s(e)} -> K_{t(e)} x M_{t(e)}, K_lambda = C^4 x V_lambda. (i) def:incidence-coefficients: the intrinsic coefficient space B_e = {(phi (x) id)(Y_e) : phi in B(K_s, K_t)^*} is coefficientSpace P e, the range of the slice map phi |-> (phi (x) id)(Y_e) (sliceLinearMap, linear in phi), hence a linear operator space and not a single residue; mem_coefficientSpace_iff is literally the set of eq:intrinsic-incidence-coefficients and coefficientSpace_eq_span_blockSlice is eq:general-incidence-expansion (B_e = span of the HS-basis coefficient blocks F_{e,a}). (ii) eq:typed-multiplicity: M_type = typedMultiplicityAlgebra P, the StarSubalgebra of Pi_lambda Matrix (M lambda) (M lambda) C cut out by R_mu B = B R_lambda and R_lambda B^H = B^H R_mu for EVERY B in B_e and every edge e (IsTypedMultiplicity; closure under +, *, 1, scalars, star proved); isTypedMultiplicity_iff_blockSlice reduces the quantifier over B_e to the finitely many coefficient-block equations. As a star-closed unital subalgebra of a finite-dimensional matrix algebra it is a unital C*-algebra on the total multiplicity carrier. (iii) iota((R_lambda)) = (+)_lambda I_{K_lambda} (x) R_lambda on the full carrier Sigma lambda, (Fin 4 x V lambda) x M lambda is multiplicityAction (multiplicative, unital, star-preserving, faithful when every V_lambda is nonempty). (iv) eq:coefficient-action-algebra: O_Y = C*(Z_lambda, B, B^* : B in B_e, e in E) on the total multiplicity carrier Sigma lambda, M lambda is coefficientActionAlgebra P := StarAlgebra.adjoin of the vertex projections Z_lambda (vertexProjection) and the corner-embedded slices blockEmbed B; it contains the generators and their adjoints and coefficientActionAlgebra_le_iff states it is the least star-closed unital subalgebra containing them (in finite dimension the algebraic star hull is the C*-hull). The earlier single-slice encoding (TypedMultiplicityAlgebra.lean) is kept as the rank-one special case.

thm:main-duality.title: Arbitrary-incidence action--multiplicity reconstruction

(ii) eq:coefficient-quiver-duality O_Y'_M = M_type and M_type'_M = O_Y on the total multiplicity carrier (coefficientActionAlgebra_commutant / coefficientCarrierAlgebra_commutant), and M_type = End Q_Y for the adjoint-closed coefficient quiver (typedMultiplicity_iff_quiverEnd: forward arrows Y_e and adjoint arrows Y_e^*, arrow spaces = spans of all functional slices; this clause is stated with Lambda, E : Type because MultiplicityQuiverArrows.QuiverEnd is). (iv) Wedderburn-coordinate independence up to the multiplicity unitaries W_l: O_Y, M_type transform by W = (+) W_l (typing_coordinate_canonicality, the corollary proved in the same file). Scoping/disclosure: the packet is given in the coordinates of its central type decomposition (as in RepresentedJointPacket: the paper only requires unitary equivalence to the displayed sum); iota is faithful when every V_l is nonempty (iotaTypedMultiplicity_faithful), so iota(M_type) is a faithful copy of M_type exactly in the paper's situation (V_l = representation spaces). Wedderburn-coordinate independence in the paper's general form (decompositions with possibly different action factors K~_l, same represented algebra as sets): typing_coordinate_canonicality_general. Audit 2 Oct 2026: the decomposition is part of def:joint-packet (J3); only the proved in-coordinates clause of thm:trinity (extInt_commutant_eq, n = 4) is used.

prop:incidence-slice-Gram.title: Slice Gram and operator--Schmidt spectrum
prop:incidence-slice-Gram.note: Proved (incidence_slice_Gram assembles). Y in B(K_s,K_t) (x) B(M_s,M_t) is a matrix Y : Matrix (K_t x M_t) (K_s x M_s) C. thm:howe-discriminant.title: Howe enhancement discriminant and generic rigidity

prop:reconstruction-error.title: Robust commutant stopping test
prop:reconstruction-error.note: TenPanel.reconstruction_error proves all three clauses in the ten-panel frame: with measured panels X̂_μ, Ŷ_μ of Hilbert–Schmidt errors ε_{X,μ}, ε_{Y,μ} and the linear reconstruction D̂_μ = (2√3/√(ϑh))(X̂_μ + iŶ_μ), K̂_e = I/√18 + Σ_μ O_{eμ} D̂_μ (reconstructedCoefficient), (i) (Σ_e ‖K̂_e − K_e ⊗ I_R‖²_HS)^{1/2} ≤ e_K := (2√3/√(ϑh))(Σ_μ (ε_{X,μ}+ε_{Y,μ})²)^{1/2} (eq:appendix-reconstruction-error, via helmert_sum_norm_sq: OᵀO = I preserves the sum of squared errors); (ii) ‖(𝒟̂ − 𝒟)x‖ ≤ 2√2 e_K ‖x‖ for the star-closed stacked commutator maps jointCommutatorL2 (starClosedStack ·) (eq:appendix-commutator-error, via ‖A‖_op ≤ ‖A‖_HS and the existing jointCommutatorL2_sub_norm_le); (iii) if 𝒟̂ has least singular value ≥ ŝ on a protected complement W (ŝ‖x‖ ≤ ‖𝒟̂x‖ for x ∈ W) and ŝ > 2√2 e_K, then no nonzero x ∈ W lies in ker 𝒟 (generic versions: robust_commutant_stopping_test also gives the lower bound (ŝ − 2√2 e_K)‖x‖ ≤ ‖𝒟x‖ and the matrix form; robust_commutant_stopping_test_ker gives ker 𝒟 = M when W = Mᗮ for a verified protected M ⊆ ker 𝒟). Disclosed conventions: the reconstruction lives on the common carrier E × R, so the true coefficient compared against K̂_e is K_e ⊗ I_R (the paper writes K_e); the 'measured least singular value ŝ on the protected complement' is formalised as the bound ŝ‖x‖ ≤ ‖𝒟̂x‖ on W (equivalently ŝ ≤ σ_min(𝒟̂|_W)); hypotheses as in prop:ten-panel-reconstruction plus OᵀO = I.

thm:word-module-recognition.title: Word-module recognition of historical internal actions
thm:word-module-recognition.note: Proved, and more generally than stated: for any unital C-algebra A (no finite-dimensionality, C*-structure or Wedderburn form needed; the statement is purely algebraic) and any family of algebra automorphisms alpha : G → (A ≃ₐ[C] A) (no group structure or finiteness of G needed), on the regular word carrier W = A with L_a = LinearMap.mulLeft, R_b = LinearMap.mulRight, U_g = (alpha g).toLinearMap: word_module_recognition states R(A)' ∩ U(G)' = L(A^G) as an equality of subsets of Module.End C A (commutants are Set.centralizer, A^G = invariantElements alpha = {a | ∀ g, alpha g a = a}, which is the fixed-point form of A ∩ {u_g}' for alpha_g = Ad(u_g)); word_module_recognition_iff is the 'equivalently' clause (T commutes with every R_b and every U_g iff T is left multiplication by a unique invariant element) and word_module_recognition_coefficient gives the coefficient T 1. The Hilbert-space structure of L^2(A, tau_reg) plays no role in the theorem and is not encoded (the carrier is the underlying vector space).

prop:word-module-defect.title: Exact module and symmetry defects

cor:word-multiplicity-firewall.title: Word-space multiplicity firewall
cor:word-multiplicity-firewall.note: Proved in the scoped form recommended by the assessor: the corollary's mathematical content is witnessed on the paper's own twelve-root benchmark (Appendix prop:word-space-inflation: E = directed edges of K_4, S_4 relabeling matrices Pm, A = M_12). word_space_multiplicity_firewall: (i) the fixed points of the conjugation representation conjRep sigma X = P X P^{-1} on the word space L^2(M_12) are exactly the invariant algebra A^{S_4} = commutantSubmodule, so the trivial-representation multiplicity on the word space is finrank = 7 (commutant_finrank_eq_seven); (ii) the trivial multiplicity on the exposed physical carrier C^E is 1 (fixed vectors = constants, via S_4-transitivity on directed edges proved by decide); hence 'multiplicity on L^2(A) need not equal multiplicity on the physical carrier'; (iii) the word-space commutant contains an M_7(C) block: m7Block is an injective multiplicative linear embedding of Matrix (Fin 7) (Fin 7) C into End(L^2(M_12)) commuting with every conjRep sigma (built from the group average E_G and End(A^{S_4}) ≅ M_7); (iv) the physical invariant algebra A^{S_4} admits no injective linear image of M_3(C) (no_M3_embedding). def:word-native-shadow.title: Word-native linear shadow

thm:external-shadow-no-go.title: Word moments cannot manufacture an external shadow
thm:external-shadow-no-go.note: Proved as a countermodel for an arbitrary finite old letter process K (h x Fin 2 resolved carrier, spectator two-level system, h nonempty). external_shadow_no_go packages: (i) both the even (clockZ) and odd (clockX) extensions recover every old word after normalized grading discard (conservative); (ii) the historical word algebras coincide literally (every extended old word is the same matrix), hence identical multiplication tables; (iii) the complete word-Gram hierarchies Tr(w1^H w2) coincide and equal twice the old Gram (trace_kronecker); (iv) all resolved entries of every historical word coincide (resolved cylinder data); (v) the proposed left-to-right grading cross block is 0 in the even extension and nonzero in the odd one; (vi)/(vii) no function of the historical word data, and no function of the word-Gram hierarchy, returns the cross block of both extensions. Scope: the grading-changing variant of the cross block is the instance exhibited (the theorem is existential, so one instance suffices); the typed-incidence variant is not separately modelled.

prop:word-space-inflation.title: Invariant word-space inflation without an internal $M_3$
prop:word-space-inflation.note: Proved. word_space_inflation, on the benchmark E = ordered unequal pairs of Fin 4 with the relabeling matrices Pm sigma: (1) the algebra generated by the point projections and the fibre averages T, H (Tm, Hm, entries 1/3 on same tail / same head) is M_12(C) (adjoin_gens_eq_top, via thm:connected-router: the support graph of the router T+H is connected, router_preconnected, explicit walks of length <= 3); (2) A^{S_4} = the commutant of the Pm sigma in A = M_12 (invariant_algebra_eq), which is isomorphic to C x M_2(C) x C x C (DegreeOneWedderburn.degreeOneCommutantEquiv); (3) the permutation character chi(sigma) = Tr Pm sigma (trace_Pm_eq_permChar; class values (12,2,0,0,0), permChar_classes) has character inner products (1/24) sum chi_lambda chi = (1,0,2,1,1) in the order (1, sgn, W, W x sgn, V_2) (physical_multiplicities); (4) the conjugation representation X -> P X P^{-1} on L^2(M_12) = M_E(C) has LinearMap.trace equal to chi(sigma)^2 (trace_conjRep, via Tr(X -> AXB) = Tr A Tr B, trace_mulLeft_comp_mulRight) with inner products (7,5,19,17,12) (conjugation_multiplicities); (5) its commutant contains an injective multiplicative M_7(C) block (WordSpaceFirewall.m7Block); (6) A^{S_4} admits no injective linear image of M_3(C). cor:historical-typed-compilation.title: Historical typed-compilation criterion
cor:historical-typed-compilation.note: Proved as the criterion the paper's proof establishes. A flat historical word hierarchy is a FlatWordTable: a finite word bank of the historical *-algebra A with its multiplication table w_i w_j = sum_k t_ijk w_k and flatness (the bank spans A, so represented elements and finite functional-calculus elements p(a) are bank combinations); the word Gram is G_ij = tau(w_i^* w_j) for the inner product <y,x> = tau(y^* x) (tau = tau_reg gives the Grand-Tensor Gram). Typed shadows are TableNativeShadow: word-native maps X -> sum c_a A_a X B_a (def:word-native-shadow) whose insertions are declared in the bank; compressions by represented typing projectors, finite symmetry/router averages and compositions are table native (compression, groupAverage, comp). The compiler `compile` reduces every inserted product in the table (eval_compile). historical_typed_compilation: (1) the ordinary, ordinary-shadow and shadow-shadow blocks of the complete mixed ancestry Gram equal explicit functions gramForm of the word Gram, the table and the declared data; (2) the Schur ancestry residual H - C^* G^dagger C (ancestryShort, spectral Moore-Penrose inverse, the display eq:table-native-short) equals its compiled form; (3) the alternating determinant shadow DetIncidence.alt of an incidence tensor compiled entrywise from typed Gram blocks equals its value on compiled entries. historical_typed_compilation_determined: two hierarchies on different algebras with the same table, Gram and declared data give the same Gram, residual and alternating shadow (no independent cross-Hankel row). Converse: external_shadow_not_compilable restates thm:external-shadow-no-go (no function of the word-Gram hierarchy returns the external cross block). Disclosed renderings: 'represented or functional-calculus elements' = bank combinations; the Store-Clifford and matter-incidence shadows = arbitrary table-native shadows; the incidence tensor entering the alternating shadow is taken entrywise from typed Gram blocks. Re-verified 30 Sep 2026: the new version adds that the same table computes the six naturality defects of thm:six-naturality when their amplitudes and tensor-leg actions are historical (and defers mixed branches to prop:naturality-compilation). Disclosed: this clause is an instance of the shadow-shadow block clause of historical_typed_compilation with the defect maps R_X, S_Y as TableNativeShadow (they are word-native maps X -> a X - X b when the tensor-leg actions are bank elements) and the amplitudes as bank words, so d_nat = sum of shadow-shadow Gram diagonal entries is table-compiled; no separate Lean statement names the naturality defects, and the mixed-branch pointer is not a claim of this corollary.

thm:connected-router.title: Connected-router full-matrix theorem
thm:connected-router.note: Proved on Matrix n n C for any finite index type n with decidable equality (nonempty for the direction full-algebra => connected, since Mathlib's SimpleGraph.Connected includes nonemptiness). C*(D_n,u) is encoded as the unital subalgebra Algebra.adjoin C (D_n ∪ {u, uᴴ}); the support graph is SimpleGraph.fromRel (u i j ≠ 0), and diagProj_mul_mul_diagProj_ne_zero_iff identifies the paper's edge condition p_i u p_j ≠ 0 with u i j ≠ 0. adjoin_eq_top_iff_connected is the boxed equivalence eq:router-full-matrix (walk induction single_mem_of_reachable + top_of_units); disconnected_block_reduction gives, for a disconnected support graph, a nonempty proper adjacency-closed component whose block projection commutes with the generated algebra (reducing subspace) and a proper block-diagonal subalgebra containing the generated algebra.

cor:one-router-minimality.title: One-router source minimality
cor:one-router-minimality.note: Proved with an explicit router on an n-dimensional carrier Fin n with diagonal minimal projections p_i = E_ii: the nilpotent cyclic shift N (N_{i,i+1} = 1, support graph the path 1-2-...-n) satisfies (i) StarAlgebra.adjoin C {p_i, N} = top = M_n(C) for every n (cyclicRouter_generates; matrix units built from p_i N p_{i+1} along the path, adjoints for the reverse direction, then WeakReset.top_of_units); (ii) N is nonnormal for n >= 2 (cyclicRouter_not_normal, N N^H != N^H N); (iii) the star algebra generated by any set of diagonal matrices, in particular by the p_i alone (no off-diagonal word), is commutative (diagonal_generated_commutative via Algebra.commute_of_mem_adjoin_of_forall_mem_commute). one_router_source_minimality packages (i)-(iii) for n = m + 2. prop:bridge-router-residuals.title: Minimal bridge and weak-router residuals
prop:bridge-router-residuals.note: Proved. Colour: delta_col(u) = ||p_H u p_T||_HS^2 + ||p_T u p_H||_HS^2 on C^3 = T + H_priv is identified with omegaCol of InternalCommutantSeedExact; with the thm:colour-bridge generators (p_T, the four private matrix units = the hypothesis that private words generate M_2(H_priv), u, u*), the generated algebra equals the reducing block algebra M_2 + C (InternalSeed.blockDiag) iff delta_col = 0, and equals M_3 iff delta_col > 0. thm:subdirect-classification.title: Finite subdirect matrix-algebra classification
thm:subdirect-classification.note: Proved (finite_subdirect_classification). Setting: B a unital star-closed subalgebra (Subalgebra + star_mem hypothesis) of the product ring Pi_{i<r} M_{n_i}(C), n_i >= 1, all coordinate projections surjective. Conclusion: there are k classes with sizes d_beta >= 1, a surjective class function cls : Fin r -> Fin k with n_i = d_{cls i} (coordinates in one class have equal matrix size; distinct sizes are never identified), and invertible V_i in M_{n_i}(C) such that x in B iff exists Y in Pi_beta M_{d_beta}(C) with x_i = V_i Y_{cls i} V_i^{-1} for all i (Y_{cls i} read in M_{n_i} through n_i = d_{cls i} via Matrix.reindex (finCongr _)); i.e. B is the diagonal embedding of one independent full matrix algebra per class, up to the inner automorphisms Ad(V_i). Infrastructure built: exists_wedderburn_pi_matrix (intrinsic Wedderburn decomposition B = Pi_beta M_{d_beta}(C) for any star-closed subalgebra of Pi_i M_{n_i}(C): transport along the block-diagonal embedding to FiniteComplexStarSubalgebraSemisimplicity.starSubalgebra_isSemisimpleRing, then Mathlib's IsSemisimpleRing.exists_algEquiv_pi_matrix_of_isAlgClosed), exists_factor_algEquiv_of_surjective (a surjective unital hom Pi_beta M_{d_beta} -> M_n kills all summands but one and is an isomorphism on it: images of the central units are scalar idempotents summing to 1; RingHom.injective out of the simple ring M_d), algEquiv_matrix_size_eq (isomorphic full matrix algebras have equal size), and NCG.matrix_algEquiv_inner (Skolem-Noether) for the inner form. thm:reciprocal-return.title: Finite reciprocal-return criterion
thm:reciprocal-return.note: Proved (reciprocal_return_criterion) at the paper's horizon n = dim N, for a finite group G with a unitary representation v (v(gg') = v g v g', v 1 = 1, v_g^* v_g = 1) whose commutant is scalar (Schur form of irreducibility), h self-adjoint, all index types finite, V nonempty. Disclosed gap: the paper's reducing projection is onto T + (V (x) Ran W_A); the Lean subspace is the (possibly larger) invariant subspace of mediator vectors from which no return word reaches H_priv, which serves the same purpose.

prop:naturality-compilation.title: Finite functional and word-moment realization
prop:naturality-compilation.note: Proved. thm:incidence-slice-cluster.title: Stable dominant coefficient space under incidence error
thm:incidence-slice-cluster.note: Proved in full. incidence_slice_cluster: for Y, Y~ : Matrix (Kt x Mt) (Ks x Ms) C with operator-Schmidt rank r (= rank of the slice map S_Y = realign Y in HS-orthonormal matrix-unit coordinates), nonzero Schmidt coefficients >= s > 0, all coefficients <= L, and ||Y~ - Y||_HS <= eps (sum of squared entry moduli <= eps^2), it proves (1) |sigma~_k - sigma_k| <= eps for all k (eq:incidence-Schmidt-Weyl, via a new Weyl inequality for Mathlib singular values and ||S_D||_op <= ||D||_HS); (2) if eps < s/2, exactly the first r coefficients of Y~ exceed s/2 (the r-dimensional dominant cluster); (3) ||H_Y~ - H_Y||_op <= eta = (2L + eps) eps; (4) if eta < s^2/2, with P = 1_(0,inf)(H_Y) and P~ = 1_[s^2/2,inf)(H_Y~) (spectral projectors of the slice Grams, H_Y = sliceGram Y = S_Y S_Y*), rank P~ = r and ||P~ - P||_op <= eta/(s^2 - eta) (eq:incidence-slice-projector). The projector bound comes from the new reusable Davis-Kahan/Riesz-type theorem hermitian_cluster_projector_perturbation (spectrum of H in {0} u [g,inf), ||H~ - H|| <= eta < g/2 => rank 1_[g/2,inf)(H~) = rank 1_(0,inf)(H) and ||difference|| <= eta/(g - eta)), proved with the paper's resolvent identity Q P~ = Q (H~ - H) P~ (H~|)^-1 on one side and a fixed-point estimate on the other, plus dimension counting for the eigenvalue localisation. Non-vacuity example included. Standard axioms only.

cor:incidence-one-sided-rank.title: One-sided operator--Schmidt rank certificate
cor:incidence-one-sided-rank.note: Proved, in the approximation-number rendering of singular values. An incidence Y in B(K_s,K_t) (x) B(M_s,M_t) is a matrix Y : Matrix (Kt x Mt) (Ks x Ms) C; its slice map S_Y (prop:incidence-slice-Gram) is the realigned matrix sliceMatrix Y as a Euclidean operator (sliceOperator), sigma_{k+1}(Y) := approximationSingularValue (S_Y) k (Eckart-Young rendering: operator-norm distance to rank <= k) and rank Y := rank of S_Y (the operator-Schmidt rank). incidence_one_sided_rank: if hsNorm (Yhat - Y) <= eps (||.||_HS = sqrt of the sum of |entries|^2) then for all k, max(sigmahat_k - eps, 0) <= sigma_k(Y), and for every N, #{k < N : sigmahat_k > eps} <= rank Y (eq:incidence-one-sided-rank). prop:compact-mosco-resolvent.title: Compact Mosco convergence implies norm-resolvent convergence
prop:compact-mosco-resolvent.note: Proved with one non-literal hypothesis. compactMoscoResolvent_general_exact: stage forms q_X(u) = ||A_X u||^2 on arbitrary Hilbert spaces H_X (graph operators A_X : D_X ->l F_X, weak resolvents R_X at a shift b > 0; paper: b = 1) transported into a common carrier H by isometries J_X; limiting form ||A u||^2 (A : D ->l F possibly unbounded) on an arbitrary Hilbert space H_inf embedded by J_inf (possibly proper), weak resolvent R_inf; hypotheses: System.TransportedMoscoConverges J J_inf q_X q_inf (def:transported-mosco (M1)/(M2)), compatibility P_X -> J_inf J_inf^* strongly, and -- in place of def:asymptotic-compactness -- a compact graph-screen tail: compact operators screen_k on H x F with sup over the embedded unit-ball graph outputs L_X(R_X f, A_X R_X f) of ||y - screen_k y|| -> 0 (this implies compact-container collective compactness and compactness of every stage resolvent; in the paper's finite-dimensional cutoff setting it follows from def:asymptotic-compactness read along subsequences, choosing A_X = L_X^{1/2} into F_X = H_X and L_X = J_X x J_X, via the energy bound for |A_X| R_X f -- this bridge is not formalised). Conclusions: R_inf compact and positive; ||J_X R_X J_X^* - J_inf R_inf J_inf^*|| -> 0; for every k the intrinsic ordered eigenvalues (Courant-Fischer values, invariant under isometric transport by courantValue_isometryConj) converge, and lambda_{k,X} = mu_k(R_X)^{-1} - b -> lambda_{k,inf} whenever mu_k(R_inf) > 0; for every circle avoiding 0 in the resolvent set of J_inf R_inf J_inf^*, the transported Riesz projections converge in norm, the limit has finite rank, and the ranks are eventually equal. Strong convergence via tendsto_compressedOperator_apply_of_transportedMosco (uses collective compactness), norm convergence via lem:collective-norm. Non-vacuity: CompactMoscoGeneralWitness.compactMoscoResolvent_general_nonvacuous (H = C^2, H_inf = C e_0). The older operatorGraphMosco_lowSpectrumConvergence_of_graphScreens (cofinal Mosco on the carrier, H_inf = H) is a special case.

lem:mosco-strong-resolvent.title: Mosco convergence gives strong transported resolvents
lem:mosco-strong-resolvent.note: Proved as stated, with no compactness hypothesis. tendsto_compressedOperator_apply_of_transportedMosco_weak: stage forms q_X(u) = ||A_X u||^2 of graph operators A_X : D_X ->l F_X on complete inner-product spaces H_X with weak graph resolvents R_X at a shift b > 0 (paper: b = 1), limiting form q_inf(u) = ||A u||^2 of a possibly unbounded A : D ->l F on a complete H_inf (weak resolvent R), embedded by isometries J_X, J_inf into a separable Hilbert carrier H (the paper's 'Let H be a separable Hilbert space'); J_inf may be a proper embedding. Hypotheses exactly: hstage, hlimit (the resolvents), hmosco = System.TransportedMoscoConverges (def:transported-mosco (M1)/(M2)), and compatibility P_X g -> Pinf g strongly for some operator Pinf (the paper has Pinf = J_inf J_inf^*; any strong limit is allowed). Conclusion: for every f, J_X R_X J_X^* f -> J_inf R J_inf^* f in norm. Proof follows the paper: ||u_X|| <= ||f||/b; along any subsequence extract a weakly convergent sub-subsequence (exists_weaklyConvergent_subsequence_of_bounded, sequential Banach-Alaoglu in the separable carrier) and one along which ||J_X u_X|| converges; (M1) along strictly increasing subsequences for weakly convergent bounded data (TransportedMoscoConverges.exists_of_strictMono_weak: gaps filled with J_X^* y, using Pinf y = y, which follows from compatibility via symmetry of Pinf, limitProjection_inner_symm) gives y = J_inf A0 with q_inf(A0) <= lim q_X(u_X); recovery sequence of u* = R J_inf^* f plus stage minimality gives F_inf(A0) <= -Re<y,f> <= F_inf(u*); strict convexity (objective gap = ||A(A0-u*)||^2 + b||A0-u*||^2) identifies A0 = u*; the same chain forces lim ||J_X u_X|| = ||y|| (weak lsc gives <=), hence strong convergence; subsequence principle. The forms are rendered as graph forms ||A_X u||^2 (closed densely defined nonnegative forms), as in the other operator-limit records. Non-vacuity: transportedMoscoWeak_nonvacuous (carrier C^2, limiting space C embedded as the proper line C e_0). Earlier compact version tendsto_compressedOperator_apply_of_transportedMosco remains valid but is no longer needed.

lem:collective-compactness.title: Asymptotic compactness gives collective compactness
lem:collective-compactness.note: Proved in the form the paper's proof establishes, on the varying-Hilbert System carrier with def:asymptotic-compactness = System.AsymptoticallyCompact / LimitFormCompact (TransportedMoscoAsymptoticCompactness.lean). Resolvent vectors R_n f = (L_n+I)^{-1} J_n^* f are encoded as minimizers of the paper's objective F_{n,f}(u) = q_n(u) + ||u||^2 - 2 Re<J_n u, f> (only the comparison with u = 0 is used, plus q_n(0) = 0 and R_n f in the form domain); this yields eq:resolvent-energy-bound as ||R_n f||^2 + q_n(R_n f) <= 8||f||^2. Then (i) for bounded sources f_n the outputs J_n R_n f_n have a strongly convergent subsequence; (ii) the transported resolvents are sequentially collectively compact (one output per stage: SeqCollectivelyCompact, which is what the paper's proofs of this lemma and of lem:collective-norm use, and which is implied by the compact-container CollectivelyCompact of VaryingHilbertCollectiveCompactness.lean); (iii) the limiting resolvent J_inf R_inf is a compact operator (from LimitFormCompact). Disclosed gap: the compact-container form of collective compactness does not follow from the paper's one-member-per-stage definition alone (counterexample q_X = X||.||^2 on a fixed infinite-dimensional H: asymptotically compact, but no stage resolvent (X+1)^{-1} I is compact); collectivelyCompact_of_seq_of_stage_compact derives it under the extra hypotheses that the sequential property holds along every strictly monotone reindexing and every stage operator is compact.

lem:collective-norm.title: Collectively compact self-adjoint convergence is norm convergence
lem:collective-norm.note: Proved on a fixed Hilbert space: a collectively compact sequence of bounded symmetric operators converging strongly to T has compact limit T and ‖T_X − T‖_op → 0. Scoped: symmetry of the limit is listed as a hypothesis in the primed version (it follows trivially from strong convergence) and the unprimed version takes compactness of T as input.

lem:low-spectrum-convergence.title: Low-spectrum convergence
lem:low-spectrum-convergence.note: Proved. New infrastructure (Analysis/CompactSelfAdjointMinMax.lean): the Courant-Fischer min-max values courantValue T k = sup_{dim V = k+1} inf_{x in V, |x|=1} re<Tx,x> of a bounded operator on an inner product space over R or C; the min-max principle gives |mu_k(A) - mu_k(B)| <= |A - B| (abs_courantValue_sub_le) and hence mu_k(R_X) -> mu_k(R_infty) under norm-resolvent convergence, exactly the paper's argument. Identification with the eigenvalues, proved without any spectral theorem: for a compact symmetric operator, a generalised Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for positive operators plus compactness produce a top eigenvector (exists_unit_eigenvector_of_sup_rayleigh), a greedy orthonormal eigenvector family e_i with T e_i = mu_i e_i and the quadratic form bounded by mu_n on the complement (exists_orthonormal_eigenvectors), and finally, for every lam > 0, #{k : mu_k = lam} = dim eigenspace(lam) (finrank_eigenspace_eq_ncard), every positive mu_k is an eigenvalue and every positive eigenvalue is some mu_k; for positive T the sequence is antitone and nonnegative. Thus mu_k is the k-th positive eigenvalue repeated with multiplicity (zero-indexed, padded by 0 beyond the rank of a finite-rank operator). lowSpectrumConvergence packages, for compact symmetric R_X -> R_infty in norm: mu_{k,X} -> mu_{k,infty} for every k; lambda_{k,X} = 1/mu_{k,X} - 1 -> lambda_{k,infty} whenever mu_{k,infty} > 0 (the limiting eigenvalue is finite); for every circle contour avoiding 0, in the resolvent set of R_infty and eventually of R_X, with uniform resolvent bounds on the contour, the Riesz projections Pi_X(Gamma) -> Pi_infty(Gamma) in operator norm and their ranks are eventually equal. Scope: the contour is a circle (the isolated finite cluster is the spectrum inside it). lowSpectrumConvergence takes the contour hypotheses (circle eventually in the stage resolvent sets, uniform resolvent bounds) as inputs; these follow from norm convergence alone by ResolventStability.exists_circle_resolvent_norm_bound and eventually_circle_resolvent_bound_of_tendsto (ContourResolventBounds.lean, as used in compactMoscoResolvent_general_exact), so the only genuine contour assumption is the paper's: the circle lies in the resolvent set of R_infty and avoids 0. Compactness and symmetry of R_X, R_infty are the paper's standing assumptions.

prop:protected-kernel-locking.title: Protected-kernel locking
prop:protected-kernel-locking.note: Proved for the paper's cofinal commutator-form setting. protectedKernelLocking_exact: stage forms q_X(B) = sum_j ||[c_{j,X},B]||_HS^2 on EuclideanSpace C (d X x d X) (bounded commutator energies, the paper's eq:cofinal-form; arbitrary closed screened forms are not covered), transported by a varying-Hilbert System J into H; limiting form q_inf(v) = ||A v||^2 of a densely defined, possibly unbounded A : D ->l F on an arbitrary Hilbert space H_inf embedded by J_inf (possibly proper), weak resolvent R at shift b > 0 (paper: b = 1); hypotheses: System.TransportedMoscoConverges (def:transported-mosco), compatibility P_X -> J_inf J_inf^* strongly, asymptotic compactness rendered as a compact graph-screen tail for the embedded stage graph resolvents (stronger as stated; in the finite-cutoff setting it follows from def:asymptotic-compactness via a suitable choice of the graph embedding L, not formalised), M_X <= Ker L_X with dim M_X = dim M_inf, Ker L_inf = M_inf (operatorGraphKernel D A = M_inf), and the added hypothesis M_inf != H_inf. Conclusions: M_inf finite dimensional; Ker L_X = M_X for late X; J_X P_{Ker L_X} J_X^* -> J_inf P_{M_inf} J_inf^* in operator norm; lambda_{m+1}(L_X) := jointCommutatorFirstPositiveGap (attained least positive eigenvalue of commutantLaplacianCLM at late cutoffs) -> gamma_inf := graphLimitComplementGap R M_inf b > 0, attained on some v in D cap M_inf^perp with ||A v||^2 = gamma_inf ||v||^2 and minimising the Rayleigh quotient on the complement. Proof via tendsto_compressedOperator_of_transportedMosco (norm-resolvent convergence), Riesz cluster rank stability and complementCompression_coercivity. Non-vacuity: protectedKernelLocking_nonvacuous (constant cutoffs diag(1,0) on 2x2 matrices, H_inf = H); no infinite-dimensional instance is exhibited.

cth:escaping-protected-mode.title: A uniformly gapped protected mode can escape
cth:escaping-protected-mode.note: Proved literally on l^2(N) = lp (fun _ : N => C) 2 with e_n = lp.single 2 n 1, M_n = C e_n, q_n[x] = ofReal ||x - P_{M_n} x||^2 (P = starProjection, eq:escaping-mode-form), on the constant varying system J_n = id with limit stage l^2(N) embedded by the identity. escapingProtectedMode_exact: q_n[x] = 0 <-> x in M_n (Ker q_n = M_n); finrank M_n = 1 (fixed protected dimension); the uniform gap q_n[x] >= 1 * ||(I - P_n)x||^2 holds with equality q_n[x] = 1 * ||x||^2 on M_n^perp (complementary gap exactly one at every cutoff); TransportedMoscoConverges id q_n q_inf with q_inf[x] = ||x||^2 (def:transported-mosco: (M1) via Banach-Steinhaus boundedness of weakly convergent sequences, weak convergence (I - P_n)x_n -> x since <e_n,x_n> <y,e_n> -> 0, and weak lower semicontinuity of the norm, transferred to ENNReal liminf; (M2) constant recovery sequences, <e_n,x> -> 0); q_inf[x] = 0 <-> x = 0 (zero limiting kernel); and the protected lines have no nonzero transported limit (any strongly convergent x_n in M_n has limit 0; no unit vectors u_n in M_n converge strongly, so the basis transport hypothesis of lem:protected-basis-transport fails).
